registered_records.found: `lam gtso'i zin bris gsang ba'i lde mig ni   (ACIP: `LAM GTZO'I ZIN BRIS GSANG BA'I LDE MIG NI,)
registered_records.evidence: Hint C01:484 verified - the backtick is present, verbatim, at the head of both the ACIP and the Wylie. But it is not stray. The same leading backtick opens 111 segments across at least 15 courses (C09 x23, C13 x19, C18 x12, C17 x9, C08 x7, C07 x6, C01 x2, and more), and in every sampled case it introduces a new text, chapter, or titled section: C02:27 '`, , gnyis pa rang gi lugs la' = 'Here is the second section'; C06:24 '`, na mo ma{u2} o ShA ya' = 'I bow down to Manjughosha'; C09:142 '`, gnyis pa ni' under the heading 'the colophon'. Here it opens the Gungtang appendix, and the English confirms a fresh text begins: 'Here is a "Secret Key to the Three Principal Paths"'.
registered_records.note: This is a structural marker in the ACIP e-text, functioning as a section/text-opening delimiter, not digitisation damage. The campaign was right to keep it verbatim and it should stay. Recommend the register carry it as a resolved non-issue so the same character is not re-flagged on later courses - C09 alone will raise it 23 more times. The trailing 'Layer: 3,747 headwords / 7,014 pairs' in the note is campaign bookkeeping and carries no claim about the text.

suspicions_all_five_grounds.suspicion: C05 English should receive the translator note found in C15/C18
suspicions_all_five_grounds.found: Here secondly is the section where we establish our own position. Now suppose three different types of beings--a pleasure being, a human, and a craving spirit, each with their own karma--sit down together and look upon a glass filled with water, the thing we define as "wet and flowing." The glass of water is not at this point one thing which is simultaneously three different objects. Neither is it necessary in this situation for there to be three identical valid perceptions. And when the glass full of wet and flowing water occurs, it occurs with three different, distinct parts to it.
